newsitem.title: UK: Jupiter says has severed links with Co-op predator.
newsitem.headline: Jupiter says has severed links with Co-op predator.

text.p: British fund management group Jupiter Asset Management (JAM) on Friday joined a growing list of City firms in distancing itself from the discredited bid by Andrew Regan's Galileo to take over the Co-operative Wholesale Society.
"Having initiated the liquidation of Galileo...it (JAM) has no further connections with any of the directors of Galileo," it said.
It had not received any papers stolen from CWS and was shocked to hear that some of the papers it had been given "may have contained information improperly obtained from CWS".
Jupiter said it was not aware of the possibility that Galileo's professional advisers may have given it papers which contained such information until after this had become public knowledge.

The 31-year-old entrepreneur Regan failed in his 1.2 billion pound ($1.9 billion) bid for the 153-year-old supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group when the Co-op got legal backing preventing the use of papers leaked by a senior CWS manager to Regan.

Jupiter is the last of three shareholders in Galileo to clarify its position. Stockbrokers Killik & Co said it had severed all links with Regan on Thursday and British investment bank Schroders which earlier said it had not seen confidential CWS papers.

Galileo, the special purchase vehicle set up by Regan to bid for the Co-op, was wound up on Wednesday but its liquidator said it had sufficient assets to repay creditors in full and enable a return to be made to shareholders. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
